title: Apple Watch heart-rate, irregular-rhythm and ECG alerts leading to arrhythmia diagnosis and treatment
summary: Apple Watch heart-rate alarms led to an ECG-confirmed AF diagnosis and anticoagulation (UK, 2019); 16 echoes from 15 published case reports to 2026.
account: In a case report of 29 March 2019 (event date not reported), a 59-year-old woman attended a United Kingdom emergency department. The acute medicine service saw her (the report does not name the hospital; the author is at Ipswich Hospital). She attended because her Apple Watch Series 2 had alarmed several times overnight that her pulse exceeded 120 bpm while she was inactive. A transient ischemic attack had occurred two months earlier. An electrocardiogram (ECG) showed atrial fibrillation with a fast ventricular response. She started bisoprolol and a direct oral anticoagulant, and clopidogrel was stopped. Later case reports describe the watch's heart-rate alerts, irregular-rhythm notification or ECG app leading to confirmed atrial flutter, supraventricular and ventricular tachycardia and heart block. Treatment was by cardioversion, ablation, pacemaker or defibrillator.
purpose: Apple Watch high/low heart-rate notifications, the Irregular Rhythm Notification and the ECG app are built to flag possible arrhythmias so the wearer seeks medical review. This benefit was that purpose.
system: Apple Watch heart-rate notifications, Irregular Rhythm Notification and ECG app
model_version: Apple Watch Series 2 (event); echoes name Series 3, 4, 5, 6 and Ultra; eight reports do not state the model, and in Ahmed et al. the alerting tracker is unnamed (the Series 5 was the authors' post-diagnosis device)

ratings.reason: One woman with a recent TIA received an ECG-confirmed AF diagnosis, rate control and anticoagulation. A material benefit to one person. Several echoes (VT ablation with defibrillator, pacemaker for heart block) are deeper but are not the event.

ai_role.statement: The watch's heart-rate algorithm generated the overnight alarms that brought the patient to hospital. Clinicians made the diagnosis on an ECG and chose treatment. data.retained_case_account: In a case report of 29 March 2019 (event date not reported), a 59-year-old woman attended a United Kingdom emergency department. The acute medicine service saw her (the report does not name the hospital; the author is at Ipswich Hospital). She attended because her Apple Watch Series 2 had alarmed several times overnight that her pulse exceeded 120 bpm while she was inactive. A transient ischemic attack had occurred two months earlier. An electrocardiogram (ECG) showed atrial fibrillation with a fast ventricular response. She started bisoprolol and a direct oral anticoagulant, and clopidogrel was stopped. Later case reports describe the watch's heart-rate alerts, irregular-rhythm notification or ECG app leading to confirmed atrial flutter, supraventricular and ventricular tachycardia and heart block. Treatment was by cardioversion, ablation, pacemaker or defibrillator.

The acute medicine service saw her (the report does not name the hospital; the author is at Ipswich Hospital). Later case reports describe the watch's heart-rate alerts, irregular-rhythm notification or ECG app leading to confirmed atrial flutter, supraventricular and ventricular tachycardia and heart block. Treatment was by cardioversion, ablation, pacemaker or defibrillator.

fields.account: In a case report of 29 March 2019 (event date not reported), a 59-year-old woman attended a United Kingdom emergency department. The acute medicine service saw her (the report does not name the hospital; the author is at Ipswich Hospital). She attended because her Apple Watch Series 2 had alarmed several times overnight that her pulse exceeded 120 bpm while she was inactive. A transient ischemic attack had occurred two months earlier. An electrocardiogram (ECG) showed atrial fibrillation with a fast ventricular response. She started bisoprolol and a direct oral anticoagulant, and clopidogrel was stopped. Later case reports describe the watch's heart-rate alerts, irregular-rhythm notification or ECG app leading to confirmed atrial flutter, supraventricular and ventricular tachycardia and heart block. Treatment was by cardioversion, ablation, pacemaker or defibrillator.
